name: Protein-yogurt pizza pittas — spelt, no-yeast (base pitta, pre-filling)

source.author: Instagram — shirel_blank / foodsdictionary_recipes (Hebrew), spelt adaptation
source.notes: Whole-spelt version of protein_yogurt_pizza_pittas — white flour swapped for whole spelt flour, everything else identical. Analyzed PER PITTA for the DOUGH BASE ONLY (pre-filling); makes 8-9, per-unit uses 8. Filling (pizza sauce, cheese, toppings) is unquantified and NOT in these macros. PRO yogurt taken as ~20 g-protein/200 g. Spelt has weaker gluten than wheat — see the cooking guide.

steps: Mix the spelt dough (go easy on water), rest, roll, stuff with sauce + cheese, pan-fry both sides.

batch_totals.note: Base dough only (8 pittas). Filling adds calories/fat/sodium on top depending on how much sauce + cheese you use.

him.verdict: The spelt swap turns the pitta base from an okay bread into a genuinely good one: ~7.1 g protein per 149 kcal pitta (spelt + the PRO yogurt) and ~3.3 g fiber — about 4x the white version's fiber — for slightly fewer calories. Whole-grain, higher protein, more filling. It's still a bread vehicle, but a strong one; the filling (cheese) remains the main calorie/sodium lever.
flags: ~3.3 g fiber (~4x the white version), whole-grain
cheese filling is the calorie/sodium lever
suggested_mods: Go light on the yellow cheese in the filling — biggest calorie/sat-fat/sodium add
Load veg toppings + the tomato pizza sauce (lycopene) to make it a fuller meal

her_preconception.verdict: Whole spelt makes this meaningfully better for her than the white base — it adds fiber, folate and a little iron on top of the yogurt's protein and calcium. Fully cooked, pasteurized yogurt, no safety flags. Contains gluten (spelt) — fine unless she's avoiding it. When filled, keep cheese pasteurized (standard) and toppings cooked.
prenatal_highlights: whole-grain fiber + a little folate & iron from the spelt
protein + calcium from the PRO yogurt
suggested_mods: Pair with a protein + veg filling to make it prenatally useful
Spelt contains gluten — fine unless she avoids it

cooking_guide: In a bowl, mix the spelt flour, baking powder and salt. Add the yogurt, olive oil and just ¼ cup cold water to start — spelt absorbs water fast, so add more only if the dough is too dry.
Stir to a shaggy dough, then knead GENTLY for ~1 min — spelt has weaker gluten than wheat, so it's softer and tears more easily; over-kneading makes it gummy. Stop as soon as it comes together.
Cover and rest 10-15 min so the flour fully hydrates — this makes the soft dough much easier to roll.
Divide into 8-9 balls. On a lightly floured surface (don't over-flour), roll each ~½ cm thick.
For the pizza version: spread a little pizza sauce and cheese on one half, fold over (or top a second round) and press the edges to seal.

Heat a pan over medium with a thin film of olive oil. Cook each pitta ~2-3 min per side until deep golden with brown spots and the cheese is melted — medium heat so the inside cooks before the outside burns.
Keep the finished pittas under a clean towel so they stay soft.
Tip: spelt browns a touch faster than white flour — watch the heat and pull them at deep golden, not dark.
